claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-015 was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the time of decision, even without proof of a logged control failure.
specific_concerns: The available record is only an actor summary, not the underlying evidence, so the audit cannot verify whether the cited items actually establish materiality rather than routine follow-up risk.

The policy says quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure; the packet relies on combining those same categories without showing why the combination crosses the material-risk threshold.
The actor explicitly characterizes support as weak, which undercuts any claim that the policy threshold is clearly satisfied.

There is no quoted or otherwise specific evidence of a formal materiality determination, approval condition, or decision rule showing that unresolved storage-control inconsistency plus process immaturity required rejection rather than conditional follow-up.

Because evidence access is actor_summary_only, there is residual concern that the rationale may be influenced by non-admissible security information even though the packet says it is not relying on it.
unsupported_claims: That the combined record definitively shows approval conditions were not met.
That the unresolved issues were materially sufficient for rejection rather than escalation or conditional approval.
That the rejection can be affirmed as compliant on the present record rather than merely plausible.
evidence_requests: Provide the full text or excerpts of BPROC-015-B, BPROC-015-C, BPROC-015-D, and BPROC-015-E.
Provide any contemporaneous procurement note or decision memo that explicitly assesses materiality and explains why rejection, rather than follow-up, was the required or chosen outcome.
Provide any logged admissible record showing the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at the exact time of decision.
Provide any policy application guidance or precedent showing that this combination of issues satisfies the 'material unresolved risk' threshold for vendor rejection.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for material unresolved risk.
Do not treat quality-process gaps or questionnaire inconsistencies alone as proof of reject-level failure, because the policy expressly says they justify follow-up or escalation.
Do not credit private security-review results unless formally logged.
Require evidence that the decision could be justified from admissible evidence alone at the time of decision, with a coherent link from facts to materiality to rejection outcome.
